This November, that spirit comes to the winery tank room in partnership with Nalla at Cliff Lede Vineyards. Experience an evening where the layered flavors of regional Indian cuisine meet the wines of Cliff Lede. Served on golden thali beneath the glow of the tanks, each course is thoughtfully paired. Along the way, you'll gain professional tips on working with fresh cheese, hear stories from the PRESS kitchen, and discover what makes gnudi a timeless staple on our menu. After class, settle in for a three-course lunch featuring the ricotta gnudi you've prepared, complemented by seasonal dishes inspired by the menus of PRESS and Under-Study. item.title: Guided Nature Walk & Ranch House tour Anderson Marsh State Historic Park — Sat Nov 14, 8:30 AM — Anderson Marsh State Historic Park
item.description:
The final Guided Nature Walk of 2026 at Anderson Marsh State Historic Park will be held on Saturday, November 14th beginning at 8:30am. The autumn season brings bright clear days and a chance to experience the fall bird migration that is in full swing at the park.
The Guided Walk will be led by State Parks volunteer docent and California Naturalist Henry Bornstein, who has been leading guided walks in the park for almost 20 years. The guided walk provides an opportunity to observe wildlife at the park and learn about their natural habitat, as well as to learn about the natural and cultural history of the area.
After the Guided Walk, there will be an opportunity to tour the historic Anderson Ranch House.
The Guided Walk will begin at 8:30am. Bring binoculars and meet in the parking lot at 8:15am for an opportunity to observe the birds and other wildlife found in the picnic area. Sturdy shoes, a hat and water are suggested.

Two sessions are offered, each featuring a different selection of holiday-inspired drinks. The November 14 class explores the perfect martini and spiced pear cider, featuring St. George gins and Spiced Pear Liqueur. The December 19 session focuses on espresso martinis and citrus punch, followed by a tasting of St. George whiskey. Both classes include guided tastings, take-home cocktail recipe cards, and a picnic lunch from Market with a choice of sandwich, chips, a Carneros cookie, and boxed water. Guests also receive an exclusive 10% discount on St. George Spirits purchases. Classes take place November 14 and December 19, from 10:30 a.m. to 12:30 p.m.

item.title: Olio Nuovo Olive Oil Celebration at Terra Sávia — Sat Nov 14, 11:00 AM — Terra Savia Winery & Olive Mill
item.description:
Due to an early harvest, olive milling went from 0-100 overnight! With milling is in full swing, November’s 2nd Saturday, the 14th has been set for our annual Olio Nuovo Celebration and Luncheon here at the mill! Olio nuovo is extra-virgin oil that’s been bottled just after milling. This is one of our favorite traditions—a chance to come together and salute our obsession with recently-milled liquid green gold, and gorge yourselves on an oil-centric meal prepared by Chef Monica. Food tickets are $35 but not required to attend and taste! We’ll also be doing regular wine tastings
Source: Press Democrat

item.title: Cookbook Club — Sat Nov 14, 12:00 PM — Sonoma Valley Library
item.description: Are you interested in trying new recipes or just wanting to get out of your cooking comfort zone? A cookbook book club blends the joy of reading with the creativity of cooking and the warmth of sharing meals. Browse a selection of themed cookbooks every month, then prepare and share your meals for the next meeting! June: Celebrating Julia in June! Julia Child & Those Influenced by Her. Before "food TV" was a genre, Julia Child was teaching America to cook-joyfully, loudly, and with plenty of permission to make mistakes. Her landmark cookbook Mastering the Art of French Cooking helped translate French technique for American home kitchens launching a whole new way of learning to cook. For this meeting, bring a dish by Julia Child or by chefs influenced by her and who share her spirit-like Jacques Pépin, her longtime cooking partner on public television, and Ina Garten, who has spoken about admiring Child's "courage of her convictions." July: Savoring Summer, Italian-Style. Think Italian

item.title: Back Care Yoga Workshop ~ Live with Greater Ease — Sat Nov 14, 1:00 PM — Revolution Yoga- Lewis Studio
item.description:
Back Care Yoga Workshop — Move with Greater Ease
"Your spine is your lifeline." — Denise Austin
Give your back the attention it deserves!
After overcoming severe sciatica and finding lasting relief, experienced yoga instructor MaryEllen Whitton created this workshop with a mission: to share the knowledge and techniques that made such a profound difference in her own life.
This workshop goes beyond the yoga mat! Discover practical strategies, simple movements, and everyday habits to improve spinal mobility, release tension, build strength, and support a healthier back.
Learn how small changes in the way you sit, stand, and move can make a meaningful difference in how you feel.
All levels welcome. No yoga experience necessary.
Leave with greater awareness and practical tools to care for your spine every day.
Source: North Bay Bohemian, Press Democrat

item.title: The (Unbelievably True) Story of Nicky O — Sat Nov 14, 1:00 PM — Rancho Cotate High School

The \(Unbelievably True\) Story of Nicky O, a new rock musical based on an incredible true story. Nicky O’Neill was an aspiring teenage rockstar when, in 2003, he became the youngest victim in the deadly Station Nightclub fire. Following his death, a series of surprising supernatural events unfolded, uniting his family & friends in the belief that Nicky is forever watching over them from above.
With original music by Nicky O’Neill and friends, alongside a brand new book by local thespian \(and Nicky’s sister-in-law\) Maureen O’Neill, Nicky O is a moving, heartfelt, and surprisingly funny message that our loved ones are never gone…they walk among us.

item.title: When Teddy Roosevelt called Jack London a "Nature Faker" — Sat Nov 14, 3:00 PM — Sonoma Valley Library
item.description:
The "nature-faker" controversy between Jack London and Teddy Roosevelt was a public argument in the press after Roosevelt accused London of anthropomorphizing animals. While these two men might have publicly debated, they actually had a lot in common. Learn about how the Roosevelt family was involved in anti-animal cruelty advocacy, including the founding of the A.S.P.C.A., how the "teddy bear" came about, and how Jack London's response to Roosevelt's criticism echoed much of what we would later understand about animal cognition. Presented by Kate Johnston, docent at the Jack London Historic State Park. Kate is a retired government attorney who writes a docent newsletter for the park. Her articles are featured on the Jack London Society webpage. jacklondonsociety.org walksandtalksbykate.com
Source: North Bay Bohemian

item.title: Lecture Two | The Social Sculpture: How Art Can Shape Society — Tue Nov 17, 7:30 PM — Laguna Lab
item.description:
As part of the 2-week art exhibition, STIMULANT, Apocalypse Studio presents the 2nd lecture in their 2-part series.
The studio’s founder spent many years working with leaders in twenty countries on some of humanity’s toughest social challenges, from war and poverty to the destruction of nature, drug abuse, immigration, and violence. He will share his insights from these years, focusing on why only the domain of culture can rebalance systemic breakdown and social decay. He will introduce what he calls the "8th great art", Social Sculpture, to add to the 7 already known (Painting, Sculpture, Literature, Architecture, Theater, Film, and Music). Social Sculpture is the art form of artfully co-creating society actively and together.
Source: North Bay Bohemian, Sebastopol Calendar

item.title: Marin Farmers Markets — Thu Nov 19, 8:00 AM — Marin Veterans' Memorial Auditorium
item.description:
Price: Free
Sponsor: Marin Center
Explore the bounty of summer at the Marin Farmers Markets. Taste vine-ripened tomatoes, corn that was picked that morning, and peaches so juicy you have to bend over just to get a bite. Farm-fresh eggs, grass-fed beef, artisan c heeses, raw milk, and freshly baked breads complete the shopping exper ience. Specialty prepared foods and handmade art add to the magic of the market.
Enjoy the intimate feeling of the Thursday Marin Farmers Market, an ideal place to meet for lunch and pick up fresh produce for the weekend. Discover the abundance and diversity of product at the celebrated Sunday Marin Farmers Market, the third largest farmers market in California. Turn your dollar into a vote for local sustainable agriculture, shrink your eco-footprint, and revive the feeling of being intimate ly connected to your food by meeting your farmers face-to-face. The market takes place rain or shine.
www.aginstitutemarin.org
Source: North Bay Bohemian, Press Dem

item.title: FSVAA 63rd Annual Nor-Cal Regional Juried Art Show — Thu Nov 19, 11:00 AM — Solano Town Center Gallery
item.description:
2026 Juried Art Exhibit: Celebrating Northern California’s Artistic Excellence!
FSVAA proudly presents the 63rd Annual Nor-Cal Regional Juried Art Show at the Solano Town Center Gallery – show opening is Friday, Nov 13. Gallery Hours are Wed thru Sun, 11am–6pm.
The three jurors, Ferdinanda Florence, Nadja Fitchhorn, and Vickie Marchand have spoken and made their selections!
We received 200 art entries from 67 talented artists representing 15 different cities throughout Northern California, making this an exciting and impressive year for our Juried Art Show.
It was wonderful to see so many artists arrive with their treasured works of art, eager to have them reviewed and considered by our three distinguished jurors.
After careful deliberation, the jurors selected 97 outstanding works of art to be included in this year's Juried Art Show!

item.title: Frank Lloyd Wright Civic Center Tours — Fri Nov 20, 10:30 AM — Civic Center
item.description:
Price: Adult $10, Senior/Full Time Student $5 \(Plus a $2 p er ticket service Charge Online\)
Ticket Info:
Sponsor: Marin Center
Link: http://www.marincounty.org/depts/cu
The Frank Lloyd Wright-designed Marin County Civic Center is a national- and state-designated historic landmark. Ninety minute docent-led tours of the Civic Center are offered every Wednesday and Friday at 10:30 am, leaving from the second floor Café, Room 233. The cost is $10 adults and $5 seniors and students. No reservations are required. Groups of ten or more can arrange a private docent tour by calling the Visitor Services Office at \(415\) 473-3762.
Source: North Bay Bohemian

item.title: Holiday Boutique — Sat Nov 21, 10:00 AM — St. Paul's Episcopal Church parish hall
item.description: St. Paul's Holiday Boutique is almost here! The sparkling event that takes place annually the Saturday before Thanksgiving begins at 10 a.m. Saturday, Nov. 21 at the St. Paul's Episcopal Church parish hall, 209 Matheson St. in Healdsburg. We offer items to streamline your holiday preparation and gift-giving, and who can't use a helping hand during this jam-packed season. Look for our wide assortment of jams, jellies, marmalade, preserves, chutneys and candies; and baked goods of all kinds including cookies, pies and breads that can be served now or frozen for later. Pick up jars of bean-soup mix to simmer and serve a crowd; and a favorite for gifting: cookie mixes that are prettily packaged; just add your own egg and butter, stir up and bake for a one-bowl batch of homemade cookies in a flash. And there are plenty of other items to make your holidays brighter: We offer a wide selection of lovely costume jewelry along with holiday decorations, housewares, serving pieces, linens and toys

item.description:
Lavender Workshop: Create, Relax & Enjoy
Spend a relaxing afternoon immersed in the soothing scent of lavender! In this hands-on workshop, you'll create your own lavender products to enjoy at home or share as thoughtful gifts.
Each participant will make and take home two lavender sprays and two lavender sugar scrubs. All materials are provided, so just bring your creativity and get ready for a fun, fragrant afternoon! Additional sprays and scrubs will also be available for purchase.
Additional sprays and scrubs will also be available for purchase.

item.title: California Redwood Chorale 20th Anniversary concerts — Sun Nov 22, 3:00 PM — Jacuzzi Family Vineyards
item.description:
The California Redwood Chorale is returning to the Jacuzzi Barrel Room to sing for you as we celebrate our 20th Anniversary.
This group of skilled singers is known for singing across the choices of choral music, from "Bohemian Rhapsody" to Mozart! This season we will honor Dolly Parton by singing her tender "Light of a Clear Blue Morning" as well as "Dirait-on" by Morten Lauridsen, "Chorale: Hymn" by Karl Jenkins, "I'll be Seeing You" by Habermann and Fain, "Ad Astra" by Narverud, "Time after Time" by Cyndi Lauper, "O Love" by Elaine Hagenberg, "The Awakening" by Martin and more!
We are so thrilled to be returning to the Barrel Room. Won't you please join us? SingChronous will be guest artists at the Jacuzzi concert.
$30 at the door cash or check to CRC
Source: North Bay Bohemian
